title: Law-student post attacks GOP deportation politics
tease: As a Yale Law student, Vance says mass deportation is unworkable and Republican proposals look “openly hostile to non-whites.”
summary: In 2012, while at Yale Law School, Vance writes that the government cannot deport millions of people and that Republican immigration proposals look “openly hostile to non-whites.” It is the clearest early contrast with the restrictionist nationalism he later runs on. He later asks a professor to take the post down.

links.label: CNN on the deleted 2012 immigration post

title: Calls Trump unfit and votes for Evan McMullin
tease: Vance brands Trump “reprehensible” and “cultural heroin,” privately wonders if he is “America’s Hitler,” and votes for Evan McMullin.
summary: During the 2016 campaign Vance is an outspoken Never Trump conservative. Publicly he calls Trump immoral, absurd, unfit, and “cultural heroin.” Privately he asks whether Trump might be “America’s Hitler.” He votes for independent Evan McMullin rather than Trump or Hillary Clinton.

links.label: Reuters on the anti-Trump-to-running-mate reversal

title: Asks a professor to delete the 2012 immigration post
tease: As Hillbilly Elegy makes him famous, Vance asks that his law-school attack on GOP immigration politics be taken down.
summary: In 2016, as Hillbilly Elegy and the Trump campaign raise his profile, Vance asks a former professor to remove the 2012 post criticizing Republican deportation politics. The request is record management, not yet a full conversion to restrictionism — that hard-line turn waits until the Senate run.

links.label: CNN on the deleted 2012 immigration post

title: Praises universities as talent and IP engines
tease: Before he calls colleges “the enemy,” Vance says they supply high-quality talent and intellectual property.
summary: In 2017 Vance still describes American universities as producers of talent and intellectual property. The later Senate campaign will quote Nixon — “the professors are the enemy” — and propose punishing endowment taxes. Paid university appearances also sit in the same years as the reversal.

links.label: Associated Press on colleges paying Vance and later attacks

title: Credits Trump with seeing Rust Belt frustration
tease: Still not MAGA, Vance begins saying Trump recognized neglected regional anger that conventional conservatives missed.
summary: By 2018 Vance has started crediting Trump with perceiving the frustration of neglected regions, even while remaining publicly outside the movement. The line is an opening, not yet an apology. Private criticism of Trump’s failure to deliver economic populism will still show up in 2020.

links.label: Washington Post profile of Vance’s radicalization

title: Pro-gun, with a limit for the clearly unstable
tease: Vance calls himself strongly pro–Second Amendment but says clearly unstable people should not have firearms.
summary: In 2018 Vance describes himself as a “big pro-Second Amendment guy” who still wants a balance. He says people who are clearly mentally unstable should not be getting firearms. Four years later his Ohio Gun Owners survey will oppose red-flag laws and adjudicative mental-health disarmament.

links.label: ABC News comparison of Vance and Walz on guns

title: Ties fatherhood and babies to civic health
tease: Vance says parenthood roots people in community and that people who think babies are bad are “sociopaths.”
summary: In 2019 Vance praises fatherhood for grounding “relatively driftless” young men and parenthood for attaching people to community and country. “We think babies are good because we’re not sociopaths.” The natalist frame — and the attack on childless elites — is already in place before he runs for office.

links.label: CNN review of childlessness remarks

title: At Ohio State, climate is a problem natural gas may not fix
tease: Vance treats climate concern as real and questions whether natural gas is an adequate answer — a line he later drops.
summary: At Ohio State in 2020 Vance expresses skepticism that natural gas is an adequate answer to climate concerns. Two years later he will say there is no climate “crisis” and that even believers should answer with more domestic fossil-fuel production. Politico later notes more than $283,000 in petroleum-industry campaign support around the reversal.

links.label: Politico on the climate shift and oil money

title: Privately, Trump still hasn’t delivered populism
tease: Even as he warms to Trump’s voters, Vance faults the president for failing to deliver economic populism and expects him to lose.
summary: In 2020 Vance still privately faults Trump for failing to deliver economic populism except for a disjointed China policy, and he expects Trump to lose. The public conversion — apology, deleted posts, MAGA identity — is the next year’s work, after he decides to run for Senate.

links.label: Washington Post profile of Vance’s radicalization

title: Apologizes to Trump and joins the MAGA lane
tease: Running for Senate, Vance apologizes for old attacks, deletes posts, and accepts Trump as the movement’s leader.
summary: After announcing a Senate bid, Vance publicly apologizes to Trump, deletes critical posts, and calls himself a “flip-flop-flipper.” He now treats Trump as the leader of a populist coalition and begins the hard-line turn on immigration, elections, and institutions. Trump will endorse him in April 2022.

links.label: Reuters on the anti-Trump-to-running-mate reversal

title: “Childless cat ladies” and extra votes for parents
tease: Vance says the country is run by miserable childless elites and floats giving parents extra votes through their children.
summary: In July 2021 Vance tells Fox News the country is “effectively run … by a bunch of childless cat ladies,” names Harris, Buttigieg, and Ocasio-Cortez, and earlier in the month floats allotting children votes that parents would cast. He also wants higher relative taxes on the childless. In 2024 he will call the cat-ladies line sarcastic but true, and back away from extra parental votes.

links.label: CNN review of childlessness remarks
ABC News on tax treatment of childless adults

title: Objects to prioritizing Afghan refugee admissions
tease: During the withdrawal Vance wants U.S. citizens first and casts unsupported suspicion on Afghan interpreters.
summary: In August 2021 Vance objects that Afghan refugees are being prioritized over Americans. In September he questions whether entrants were truly interpreters and alleges, without evidence, that many ostensible helpers assisted roadside-bomb attacks. The page records no Afghan-specific bill or vote of his.

links.label: Associated Press on the split over Afghan refugees
Guardian reporting on the 2021 podcast remarks

title: Op-ed: Ohio State’s vaccine mandate invades medical privacy
tease: Vance writes that a university COVID vaccine requirement is an outrageous invasion of medical privacy.
summary: On August 27, 2021, Vance publishes a Columbus Dispatch op-ed attacking Ohio State University’s COVID vaccination requirement as an invasion of medical privacy. Two years later, as a senator, he will introduce the Freedom to Breathe Act to bar federal mask mandates on airlines, transit, and public schools.

links.label: Columbus Dispatch op-ed on Ohio State’s vaccine mandate

title: Rejects rape and incest exceptions: “two wrongs don’t make a right”
tease: Vance prefers asking whether a child should live, likens abortion’s social effects to slavery, and skips rape and incest exceptions.
summary: In September 2021 Vance says abortion laws should not carve out rape and incest because “two wrongs don’t make a right.” A month later he says abortion’s social effects are comparable to slavery. At Claremont he argues companies favor abortion to preserve cheap labor. The national-illegality line is still a few months away.

links.label: Washington Post on rape and incest exceptions

title: Calls for “de-woke-ification” of American institutions
tease: Vance’s “Fighting Woke Capital” line treats business, media, and philanthropy as a progressive bloc that conservatives must purge.
summary: In 2021 Vance argues that business, finance, academia, media, and philanthropy form a progressive institutional bloc. Conservatism, he says, must become a “counterrevolutionary force,” with a “de-woke-ification” he analogizes to denazification. Universities, already praised in 2017, are recast as hostile institutions.

links.label: Vance’s “Fighting Woke Capital” essay

title: Tells Trump to fire the civil service and defy the courts
tease: Vance’s advice: replace midlevel bureaucrats with loyalists, and if judges intervene, let them try to enforce the ruling.
summary: In 2021 Vance advises a future Trump administration to fire civil servants, replace them with loyalists, and, if courts block the purge, invoke Andrew Jackson: the chief justice “has made his ruling, now let him enforce it.” The line is a theory of executive supremacy, not a statute. He will repeat a version of it as vice president.

links.label: Vox analysis of Vance’s executive ideas

title: Wants abortion “illegal nationally,” with a federal backstop
tease: Vance says he would “certainly” like abortion illegal nationwide and is sympathetic to stopping Ohioans from traveling out of state.
summary: In January 2022 Vance says he would “certainly” like abortion to be illegal nationally. He is “pretty sympathetic” to a federal response if a post-Roe Ohio ban were undercut by people flying to California. The statement, not a bill, is the high-water mark of a national ban. In 2024 he will say he never supported one.

links.label: CNN on the 2022 national-illegality statement
NBC News chronology of six abortion statements

title: Ohio Gun Owners survey: abolish ATF, no red-flag laws
tease: The 2022 candidate survey backs repealing the National Firearms Act and opposes red-flag laws and the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
summary: During the Senate primary Vance tells Ohio Gun Owners he supports abolishing ATF, repealing the National Firearms Act and Gun-Free Schools Act, a national stand-your-ground law, and a Second Amendment Preservation Act. He opposes red-flag laws, private-sale background checks, semi-automatic bans, and the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act. Survey answers are commitments, not votes.

links.label: Ohio Gun Owners candidate survey

title: Trump endorses Vance for Senate
tease: The conversion is consummated: Trump’s endorsement locks Vance into the MAGA lane he spent 2016 denouncing.
summary: In April 2022 Trump endorses Vance in the Ohio Senate race. The endorsement follows the apology, the deleted posts, and the new hard line on immigration and elections. It is the public seal on a reversal that began when Vance decided electoral politics required MAGA rather than Never Trump conservatism.

links.label: Reuters on the anti-Trump-to-running-mate reversal

title: Claims the FBI illegally wiretapped Trump
tease: Vance alleges illegal FBI surveillance of Trump. Fact-checks find the wiretap claim false; “defund” meant ATF, not all policing.
summary: On the 2022 trail Vance alleges the FBI illegally wiretapped Trump and took part in pre-2020 censorship. Reporting finds the wiretap claim false. A separate “defund law enforcement” fight is specifically about abolishing ATF, not city police. The deep-state frame for DOJ and FBI is now a campaign theme.

links.label: Business Insider on the FBI wiretap claim
PolitiFact on what Vance proposed defunding

title: Ditches earlier support for Social Security cuts
tease: Reporting during the Senate race says Vance has abandoned a past willingness to cut Social Security.
summary: During the 2022 Senate campaign, reporting says Vance has ditched earlier support for Social Security cuts. By 2024 he opposes cuts and privatization and pairs Social Security and Medicare as programs Trump would protect, arguing higher labor-force participation and birth rates can keep the system solvent.

links.label: HuffPost on abandoning support for cuts

title: Opposes the Respect for Marriage Act
tease: Vance says marriage is a man and a woman and opposes federal codification of same-sex marriage. The act becomes law anyway.
summary: In the 2022 Senate race Vance opposes the Respect for Marriage Act. He says marriage is between a man and a woman but does not treat overturning existing marriages as an immediate priority. The act still becomes law. In 2023 he will add a federal felony proposal for specified gender-transition surgery on minors.

links.label: Columbus Dispatch on opposition to the Respect for Marriage Act

title: No climate “crisis” — drill more at home
tease: Vance now rejects a climate crisis and says even believers should answer with more domestic fossil-fuel production.
summary: By the 2022 Senate race Vance says he does not believe there is a climate crisis. Even those who do, he argues, should respond with more U.S. fossil-fuel production rather than offshoring manufacturing. The 2020 Ohio State concern about natural gas is gone. A 2023 bill will try to kill Inflation Reduction Act EV credits.

links.label: Cleveland.com candidate issue questionnaire
Politico on the climate shift and oil money

title: Holds Biden DOJ nominees after Trump’s indictment
tease: After the classified-documents case, Vance announces procedural holds on Justice Department nominees — a Senate tactic, not just a speech.
summary: In June 2023, after Trump’s classified-documents indictment, Senator Vance announces holds on Biden Justice Department nominees. The tactic affects unrelated appointments. He has already called DOJ the most out-of-control deep-state component and wants culturally aligned prosecutors.

links.label: NBC News on holds against DOJ nominees

title: Bill to make some gender-transition surgery on minors a felony
tease: Vance proposes federal criminal penalties for specified gender-affirming surgery on minors and a “Passport Sanity Act.”
summary: In July 2023 Vance introduces legislation to make specified gender-transition surgery on minors a federal felony and to block taxpayer funds. He also proposes the Passport Sanity Act against an “X” marker and later objects to gender-identity questions on the census. Neither bill is described as enacted.

links.label: Cleveland.com on the minor-transition-care bill

title: Proposes a 35% tax on large university endowments
tease: Vance wants the endowment tax raised from 1.4% to 35% for covered secular private colleges, plus foreign-gift enforcement.
summary: In 2023 Vance introduces a proposal raising the endowment-income tax from 1.4% to 35% for certain secular private institutions, plus foreign-donation enforcement. After the affirmative-action ruling he demands university records for a possible congressional probe. Neither tax bill is described as advancing.

links.label: Inside Higher Ed on his university agenda
Cleveland.com on probing affirmative-action compliance

title: Introduces a bill to make English the official U.S. language
tease: The official-English bill is part of the restrictionist turn that began in the Senate campaign. Introduction is not enactment.
summary: In 2023 Vance introduces legislation to make English the official language of the United States. It sits alongside the border-wall, no-amnesty, and mass-deportation program he adopted after 2021. Like most of his Senate bills in this archive, it is an introduced proposal, not enacted law.

links.label: NPR guide to Vance’s major positions

title: Freedom to Breathe Act would bar federal mask mandates
tease: The bill would block federal mask rules on airlines, transit, and schools and stop those providers from refusing unmasked customers.
summary: In September 2023 Vance introduces the Freedom to Breathe Act, which would bar federal mask requirements on airlines, transit, and public schools and prevent those providers from refusing service to unmasked people. He calls mask mandates unscientific. The bill is introduced; no enactment is documented here.

links.label: WLWT on the federal anti-mask-mandate bill

title: Bill to kill EV credits and subsidize U.S. gasoline cars
tease: Vance proposes eliminating specified IRA electric-vehicle credits and creating a $7,500 credit for U.S.-made gasoline cars.
summary: Vance introduces legislation to eliminate specified Inflation Reduction Act EV credits and to create a $7,500 credit for U.S.-made gasoline vehicles. A related pitch ties EV-credit repeal to ending the EITC marriage penalty. The bills are proposals, not enactments, and they complete the climate reversal that began in 2022.

links.label: The Hill on eliminating EV tax credits

title: Sides with striking UAW workers
tease: Vance’s public strike support is unusual for a Republican, even as he opposes the PRO Act and draws a 0% AFL-CIO score.
summary: During the 2023 UAW strike Vance publicly supports the workers, a rare Republican pose, while still attacking some union leadership. He prefers American Compass-style worker councils and sectoral bargaining to the PRO Act. The AFL-CIO later scores his Senate voting record at 0%, so the pro-labor brand and the roll-call record split.

links.label: Politico on Vance’s labor-populist project
CNN on skepticism from pro-worker groups

title: Would “absolutely not” authorize force against Iran
tease: After Iran-linked militia attacks, Vance says military action would be a mistake and he would not vote to authorize it.
summary: In October 2023 Vance says a U.S. military response after Iran-linked militia attacks would be a mistake and that he would “absolutely not” authorize force. The anti-entanglement line is the one he ran on. In 2025 he will defend strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, and in 2026 a war.

links.label: The Hill on opposing authorization of force in 2023

title: Questions bank CEOs on “woke” DEI commitments
tease: In a Senate hearing Vance treats Wall Street DEI pledges as politicized finance. A question is oversight, not a new rule.
summary: On December 6, 2023, Vance questions bank CEOs about DEI commitments and politicized finance. The hearing is the oversight face of the 2021 “woke capital” essay. It does not, by itself, change regulation. The target list — Harvard, philanthropy, banks, corporate DEI — is the same institutional map.

links.label: Senate office release on questioning bank CEOs

title: Says Ukraine should cede land and stay out of NATO
tease: Vance wants a negotiated freeze: territorial concessions, neutrality, and no restoration of the 1991 borders.
summary: By late 2023 Vance says Ukraine should cede territory and that manpower and munitions constraints make a negotiated peace the realistic outcome. He has already said he does not “really care” what happens to Ukraine next to fentanyl deaths at home, and he recycles unaudited yacht-corruption tropes that reporting traces to propaganda.

links.label: NBC News on territorial concessions
New York Times collection of Vance’s Ukraine statements

title: Stay in NATO — if Europe pays and America looks to China
tease: Vance says the U.S. should not leave NATO, but Europeans must spend more as Washington pivots toward East Asia.
summary: In February 2024 Vance says the United States should not leave NATO, provided Europeans carry more of their own defense while the U.S. focuses on China and Taiwan. At Munich he calls East Asia the next 40 years’ central American problem. Ukraine aid, in this frame, is a diversion of weapons and attention.

links.label: The Hill on NATO and Europe
Voice of America on China as “biggest threat”

title: Votes against Ukraine aid and writes that more money cannot win
tease: Vance’s New York Times essay says virtually no continued-funding proposal can change the war’s trajectory.
summary: In April 2024 Vance votes against a Ukraine aid package and publishes a New York Times essay arguing that more American money will not restore the 1991 borders. He prefers a fortified freeze near current lines, Ukrainian neutrality, and limited long-term security help. He says he does not want Russia to conquer the country.

links.label: Vance’s New York Times essay opposing further aid

title: Arm Israel, stop “micromanaging,” finish Gaza quickly
tease: Vance wants Israel aid unbundled from Ukraine aid and criticizes Biden for withholding precision weapons.
summary: Through spring and summer 2024 Vance argues that the United States should arm Israel to end the Gaza war quickly, then revive Israel–Sunni alignment against Iran. He blasts Biden for “micromanaging” and withholding munitions, and says Hamas bears responsibility for civilian deaths. He still warns that U.S. and Israeli interests can diverge on Iran.

links.label: Times of Israel on ending Gaza war and Sunni alignment
Senate office statement on Biden’s Israel policy

title: Calls youthful support for the Iraq War a mistake
tease: Vance says the foreign-policy establishment misled him into backing the 2003 invasion he now treats as a cautionary tale.
summary: By 2024 Vance publicly recants his support, as a young Marine, for the Iraq invasion. He says the establishment sold a false bill of goods. In 2025 he will call the war a strategic disaster and use it to argue that a more independent Europe might have constrained Washington’s interventionism.

links.label: Politico on Republican veterans and anti-interventionism

title: Trump’s running mate: tariffs, antitrust, keep the ACA
tease: The VP pick packages economic nationalism: break up Google, praise Lina Khan, stay open to a weaker dollar, and not repeal Obamacare.
summary: Trump names Vance as his running mate. The economic packet is already in view: tariffs and reshoring, a higher minimum wage, openness to a weaker dollar, a merger-tax bill with Sheldon Whitehouse, and praise for FTC chair Lina Khan. He also says he does not intend to repeal the Affordable Care Act and has co-sponsored an insulin cap.

links.label: NPR analysis of Vance’s economic policy
The Hill on praise for Lina Khan

title: Jokes that Labour Britain could be an “Islamist” nuclear state
tease: British officials reject the crack. Vance still describes a working friendship with Labour’s David Lammy.
summary: After Labour’s 2024 victory Vance jokes that Britain might become the first “truly Islamist” country with nuclear weapons. UK officials reject the characterization. The diplomatic relationship is messier than the line: he and Foreign Secretary David Lammy later describe each other as friends.

links.label: Politico Europe on the “Islamist country” remark
BBC on British officials’ response

title: Praises Orbán’s “smart” takeover of universities
tease: On Face the Nation, Vance calls Viktor Orbán’s university interventions smart and says the American left’s hold requires a political answer.
summary: Vance tells Face the Nation that Viktor Orbán made “smart decisions” on Hungarian universities and that U.S. higher education needs a political solution because left-wing foundations control the sector. It is an explicit rejection of institutional neutrality, completing the arc from 2017 praise to “the professors are the enemy.”

links.label: CBS News on praise for Orbán’s university decisions

title: Mifepristone access, states decide, veto a national ban
tease: After Trump, Vance backs continued mifepristone access and says a President Trump should veto a congressional national ban.
summary: In June–August 2024 Vance follows Trump toward state decision-making on abortion, says he supports access to mifepristone, and tells Laura Ingraham that Trump should veto a national ban if Congress sent one. He also proposes a $5,000 child tax credit and retreats from extra votes for parents. The 2022 national-illegality tape is still on the internet.

links.label: NBC News on the national-ban veto
CBS News on the $5,000 child tax credit

title: After a Georgia shooting, school shootings are a “fact of life”
tease: Vance rejects new gun laws and wants more school security. He has already called a bump-stock ban a PR distraction.
summary: The day after a Georgia high-school shooting, Vance says school shootings are “a fact of life,” will not be stopped by stricter gun laws, and should be answered with more school security. Earlier in 2024 he called bump-stock legislation a “huge distraction” aimed at a PR problem.

links.label: CNN on “fact of life” and school security

title: Spreads Springfield pet-eating claims, then says he will “create stories”
tease: City and police find no credible pet-eating reports. Vance is willing to “create stories” to force attention onto Haitian migrants.
summary: Vance amplifies claims that Haitian migrants in Springfield, Ohio, ate pets. City and police officials say there are no credible reports and note that many Haitians are legally present under TPS. He acknowledges rumors may be false, then says he is willing to “create stories” to get media attention, and still calls protected migrants “illegal aliens.”

links.label: New York Times on “create stories”
NBC News on Springfield officials disputing pet claims

title: Debate: never a national ban, Trump “salvaged Obamacare,” won’t say he lost
tease: Vance claims he never supported a national abortion ban, misstates Trump’s ACA record, and will not say Trump lost in 2020.
summary: At the October 1 vice-presidential debate Vance says he “never supported a national ban” on abortion, contrary to the 2022 recording. He says Trump “salvaged Obamacare,” which fact-checkers call false: Trump sought repeal in 2017. He also evades whether Trump lost in 2020; footage soon shows him saying Trump won. Alternate-elector talk remains his 2024 position.

links.label: Washington Post vice-presidential-debate fact-check
NBC News on refusal to acknowledge the 2020 result

title: U.S. and Israeli interests diverge on a war with Iran
tease: Vance still wants Israel armed, but says America should stay out of a war with Iran — a limit he will not keep.
summary: In October 2024 Vance explicitly says America’s interests sometimes differ from Israel’s, especially in avoiding war with Iran. He had praised the Soleimani killing and said that if the U.S. hits Iran it should “punch them hard,” a limited-force caveat. The 2025 strikes and 2026 war sit on the other side of that limit.

links.label: Washington Examiner on distinct U.S.–Israel interests

title: Defends Musk’s AfD line, then says he is “not endorsing”
tease: Vance will not endorse Alternative for Germany, but he amplifies favorable arguments and rejects the “Nazi-lite” tag.
summary: In December 2024 Vance sarcastically attacks criticism of Elon Musk’s AfD support. In January 2025 he says he is “not endorsing” any German party, then calls Musk’s “Only the AfD Can Save Germany” essay interesting and offers a historical argument favorable to the party. It is diplomatic rhetoric, not U.S. legislation.

links.label: Independent on his response to Musk’s AfD essay

title: Backs blanket clemency for January 6 defendants
tease: As vice president Vance supports Trump’s broad January 6 pardons. The clemency is presidential; his role is public advocacy.
summary: In January 2025 Vance is reported as backing Trump’s blanket clemency for January 6 defendants. Trump’s pardons are enacted presidential action; Vance’s documented role is advocacy and defense. A year later he will mock a vigil commemorating the attack.

links.label: Axios on broad January 6 pardons
Washington Post on election denial and January 6

title: Judges “cannot control the executive’s legitimate power”
tease: As vice president Vance says courts may not tell generals how to fight or attorneys general how to prosecute.
summary: On February 10, 2025, Vance says judges may not tell generals how to conduct operations or attorneys general how to exercise prosecutorial discretion, and therefore cannot control “the executive’s legitimate power.” Critics hear a denial of judicial review. The qualifier “legitimate” leaves unresolved who decides legality — the 2021 Jackson line in office.

links.label: Guardian on the 2025 judicial-power statement

title: Defends Trump tariffs as self-reliance and defense production
tease: Vance’s job is public defense of enacted administration tariffs, not independent authorship of the program.
summary: As vice president Vance defends the Trump administration’s tariffs as necessary for self-reliance and defense production. The policy is enacted White House action; his quoted role here is advocacy. It is the governing face of the economic nationalism he had described since the Senate campaign.

links.label: Washington Post on Vance and Republican business elites

title: Calls Europe a U.S. “security vassal” and Iraq a disaster
tease: Vance says greater European independence might have helped avert Iraq, which he now calls a strategic disaster.
summary: In April 2025 Vance calls Europe a permanent U.S. “security vassal” and argues that a more independent Europe might have constrained the Iraq War. He now describes that invasion as a strategic disaster. The burden-sharing demand is consistent; the Iraq lesson is the public recantation of his youthful support.

links.label: Deutsche Welle on European independence and Iraq

title: Defends U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites
tease: Vance argues Trump hit a bounded objective and will avoid a long war — a claim that will not survive 2026.
summary: In June 2025 Vance supports U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, arguing that Trump achieved a limited objective and would not repeat the long wars Vance spent years opposing. The “punch them hard” caveat from 2024 is now an enacted operation. A war defense follows the next year.

links.label: CBS News on defending the 2026 Iran war

title: Mocks a vigil commemorating January 6
tease: A year after backing blanket clemency, Vance ridicules a commemoration of the Capitol attack.
summary: In January 2026 Vance mocks a vigil commemorating the January 6 attack, after having backed Trump’s blanket clemency the previous year. The sequence — deny the 2020 result, refuse ordinary certification, pardon the rioters, mock the memorial — is the end of the Never Trump years, not a separate conversion.

links.label: Axios on broad January 6 pardons

title: Defends Venezuela strikes and “stolen oil” recovery
tease: Vance casts action against Nicolás Maduro as hunting a U.S.-wanted fugitive, not a new forever war.
summary: In 2025–26 Vance defends U.S. strikes connected to Nicolás Maduro, calling him a U.S.-wanted fugitive and saying “stolen oil” must be returned. Barron’s reports that Trump had offered Maduro multiple off-ramps. The archive has no earlier Vance-specific Venezuela record, so the trajectory is thin and the recent claim needs independent confirmation.

links.label: Barron’s on Vance, Maduro, and off-ramps

title: Defends the Iran war after years of anti-interventionism
tease: The most conspicuous break with Vance’s realist, anti-entanglement identity is now a war he is willing to own.
summary: In 2026 Vance defends the Iran war despite years of arguing that America should stay out. He distinguishes “smart,” limited Trump operations from Iraq-style occupations, but support for an actual war collides with the 2023 “absolutely not” and the October 2024 warning that U.S. and Israeli interests diverge on Iran. A CBS video report is the cited source.

links.label: CBS News on defending the 2026 Iran war
